subject: Re: Data residency (EU) + DPA and subprocessor list request
body:
From: Sofia Keller <sofia.keller@alpenbank.eu>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 18 Feb 2026 09:12:34 +0100
Subject: Data residency (EU) + DPA and subprocessor list request

Hi Hannah,

Following yesterday’s call, our InfoSec and Privacy teams have a few specific questions before we can move forward:

1) Data residency: If we use the hosted Redwood API, can you confirm that prompts/outputs and any derived data are stored and processed in the EU only?
2) Logging: Do any logs containing request payloads or identifiers leave the EU? Where is telemetry processed?
3) Retention: What are your default retention periods for application logs and audit logs?
4) Subprocessors: Please provide a current list of subprocessors (including cloud providers) and the region(s) involved.
5) DPA: Please share your standard DPA template and the process to execute.

If you have a one-pager that summarizes the EU posture, that would be helpful for our internal review.

Thanks,
Sofia

Sofia Keller
Vendor Risk & Privacy
AlpenBank AG

Hi Sofia,

Thanks — this is clear.

A couple quick clarifiers so I can get you the most accurate answers (and avoid over-committing in writing):

- Which deployment mode are you evaluating (Hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private/VPC)?
- Are you specifically targeting an EU-only setup (both processing and storage), or is EU processing + restricted retention sufficient?
- For identifiers: are you referring to customer account metadata (org name, billing contacts) or request-level identifiers (request IDs, IPs)?

I’m pulling the latest approved data residency one-pager + subprocessor list and will also loop in our GRC team for the DPA template and the standard evidence-sharing process.

Best,
Hannah

Hi Hannah,

We are currently looking at Hosted API for a pilot, with an EU-only requirement for processing. For storage: EU-only strongly preferred, but we can review exceptions if limited to operational logs.

Identifiers: request-level identifiers (request IDs, IP, any customer-provided user IDs in headers) are the main concern.

On DPA: we use our own template sometimes, but first would like to review yours. We will likely need SCCs if there is any cross-border processing.

Thanks,
Sofia

Hi Olga/Daniel — looping you in for approved responses.

Prospect (AlpenBank AG, EMEA) is evaluating Hosted API. They’re asking for:
- EU-only processing confirmation
- Whether any logs/telemetry containing payloads/identifiers leave EU
- Retention defaults (app logs + audit logs)
- Current subprocessor list + regions
- Our standard DPA template + process (they mentioned SCCs if any cross-border processing)

Can you please provide:
1) Approved wording for Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (if we want to proactively include the distinction)
2) What we can share directly vs what requires NDA / the evidence process
3) Latest subprocessor list artifact and whether there’s a customer-facing version

They explicitly care about request IDs, IPs, and any customer-provided IDs in headers.

Thanks,
Hannah

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Daniel Carter <daniel.carter@redwoodinference.com>; Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 19 Feb 2026 09:14:07 +0100
Subject: Re: FW: AlpenBank AG — EU data residency + DPA/subprocessor request (need approved language)

Hi Hannah,

Approved guidance below (please keep wording close to this; avoid “always/never”):

EU processing / residency (Hosted API):
- We can support EU-region processing for Hosted where available. Customers can select an EU region for inference request processing.
- Data flows and control surfaces differ by deployment mode; Dedicated and Private provide stronger controls around network boundaries and data flow.

Logs / telemetry:
- Do NOT state that “no identifiers ever leave the EU.” Instead: we separate operational telemetry from customer content; we do not use customer prompts/outputs to train models.
- For content logging: default is not to log request/response bodies beyond what is required for service delivery and troubleshooting; any diagnostic logging is access controlled and time-bound.
- If they need strict controls, position Dedicated/Private as the right fit.

Retention:
- Use the retention one-pager language; do not invent periods. If asked for exact days and it’s not in the customer-facing doc, route back to GRC.

Subprocessors:
- Share the customer-facing subprocessor list PDF. If they request SOC 2 report or pen test summaries, that’s NDA-gated and requires us to track distribution.

DPA:
- We can provide our standard DPA template for review. Execution is via our legal team once there is a confirmed commercial path (or earlier if it’s gating procurement). If they want to use their template, that’s common; we review and redline.
- Do not promise SCCs unconditionally; say we can support appropriate transfer mechanisms where required and confirm during legal review.

Daniel attached the latest customer-facing subprocessor list and the EU data residency one-pager.

Thanks,
Olga

Olga Petrov
GRC / Compliance
Redwood Inference

Hi Sofia,

Sharing the latest customer-facing materials to support your internal review:

Attachments:
- Redwood_Inference_Data_Residency_One-Pager_v2.0.pdf
- Redwood_Subprocessors_List_2026-02.pdf

High-level answers (Hosted API, EU region):

1) Data residency / EU processing
- For our Hosted API, customers can select an EU region for inference request processing where available. The attached one-pager outlines the region options and how data flows differ across Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private.

2) Logging / telemetry (and whether anything leaves the EU)
- We separate operational telemetry from customer content. We do not use customer prompts/outputs to train models.
- For strict “EU-only” requirements (including tight control over networking and operational data flow), many regulated customers choose Dedicated capacity in-region or a Private deployment (VPC/on-prem). If you can share your exact requirement boundaries, we can recommend the right mode for the pilot.

3) Retention
- The one-pager references our retention defaults and the levers available by deployment mode. If you need a written statement for a specific retention period for your policy mapping, I can coordinate that with our compliance team.

4) Subprocessors
- Included as an attachment. If your team needs additional compliance evidence (e.g., SOC 2 report), we can share via our standard evidence process (typically under NDA and with distribution tracking).

5) DPA
- We can provide our standard DPA template for review and coordinate execution with our legal/compliance team. If AlpenBank prefers to use your DPA, that’s also common — we’ll review and redline accordingly.

If helpful, I’m happy to set up a 30-minute working session with your Privacy + InfoSec stakeholders to walk through Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private boundaries for EU-only requirements.

Best regards,
Hannah

Hannah Schmitt
Account Executive, EMEA
Redwood Inference
